report.summary: Most kill criteria are falsifiable but some are vague or lack specific thresholds, and the leakage list mixes checkable and uncheckable items; overall the section is actionable but needs tighter definitions.
risks: 13.1 | medium | 'does not beat code-only or BM25 retrieval' lacks a significance threshold and baseline reproducibility; any observed difference might be dismissed as noise | Run 10 seeds with identical compute budgets, define a minimum effect size (e.g., 5% improvement) and a statistical test (e.g., paired bootstrap) to declare a kill.

13.2 | medium | 'perform equivalently' lacks a definition of equivalence; any difference could be argued as non-equivalent | Pre-specify an equivalence margin (e.g., within ±2% of each other on the primary metric) and test with a two-one-sided test (TOST) at α=0.05.

13.4 | medium | 'no marginal contribution in ablation' lacks a threshold for 'no marginal contribution'; a trivial contribution could be argued as non-zero | Define a minimum marginal gain (e.g., <1% absolute improvement) below which the plane is considered non-contributing.

13.6 | medium | 'does not beat random or evaluator-only choice' lacks a significance criterion; random baselines can vary | Pre-register a fixed random seed or distribution, define a minimum improvement (e.g., 5%) and use a statistical test with multiple trials.

13.7 | medium | 'disappears after temporal and knowledge-leakage scrubbing' is vague because 'disappears' is not quantified and scrubbing procedures are not specified | Explicitly define the scrubbing protocol (e.g., remove all post-cutoff data, hold out last 20% of timeline) and set a threshold (e.g., gain drops below 1%).

13.8 | medium | 'extra context tokens explain the whole gain' is ambiguous: what counts as 'explain the whole gain'? | Conduct an ablation where context tokens are replaced with random tokens of equal length; if performance remains the same, the gain is explained by context tokens.

13.9 | medium | 'worsens the quality/cost frontier' lacks a metric for 'frontier'; cost and quality are multi-objective | Define a composite cost-quality metric (e.g., quality per unit cost) and a threshold (e.g., >10% worse) for a kill.

13.10 | medium | 'cannot be maintained at usable cost' is subjective; 'usable cost' is undefined | Define a maximum acceptable cost per snapshot (e.g., <1% of total compute budget) and a latency target.

13.11 | medium | 'cannot achieve useful precision after verification cost' is vague; 'useful precision' and 'verification cost' are not quantified | Define a minimum precision (e.g., >90%) and a maximum cost (e.g., <10% of query budget) that must both be met.

13.12 | medium | 'benefits disappear on held-out repositories, under equal context budgets, or in cross-project transfer' lacks a definition of 'disappear' and specific thresholds | Define a minimum effect size (e.g., 5% improvement) and require that at least two of three conditions show no significant gain.

13.13 | low | 'seal the evaluator from the candidate' is a good practice but not a claim that can be falsified; it is a methodological instruction | Ensure the instruction is followed; it is not a kill criterion.
13.14 | low | 'use identical problem definitions and compute/token budgets' is a methodological requirement, not a falsifiable claim | Verify compliance; not a kill criterion.
13.15 | low | 'cover multiple task classes' is a recommendation; not falsifiable | Define what constitutes 'multiple' (e.g., at least 3 distinct task types).
13.16 | low | 'run at least 5–10 seeds when stochastic variance matters' is a guideline; not a falsifiable claim | Ensure the guideline is followed; not a kill criterion.

13.17 | low | 'Report algorithm quality, sample efficiency, repository evolution, and product reliability separately' is a reporting requirement; not falsifiable | Ensure the report includes these metrics.

13.18 | low | 'Reject results when code, prompts, memory, model, search policy, and evaluator changed together' is a methodological rule; not a falsifiable claim | Verify that changes are isolated; not a kill criterion.

13.19 | medium | 'Prevent leakage from gold patches, private tests, post-cutoff issue/commit text, post-task graph edges, previous solutions in adaptive memory, base/candidate snapshot mixing, evaluator paths or outputs, and model-generated hypotheses re-entering the Knowledge plane as facts' is a list of leakage sources; some are checkable (e.g., gold patches) but others like 'model-generated hypotheses re-entering the Knowledge plane as facts' are vague and hard to verify | For each source, specify a concrete detection method (e.g., hash comparison for gold patches) and define 're-entering' as a measurable event.
todos: Define quantitative thresholds for each kill criterion (e.g., minimum effect size, equivalence margin).
Specify the scrubbing protocol for temporal and knowledge leakage.
Define 'usable cost' and 'useful precision' with concrete numbers.
Clarify what 'explain the whole gain' means operationally.
Convert methodological instructions (non-falsifiable) into separate compliance checks, not kill criteria.

claims.claim: Stop or redesign when the full representation does not beat code-only or BM25 retrieval.
claims.why: Falsifiable in principle, but lacks a significance threshold and baseline reproducibility. Without a pre-specified minimum effect size and statistical test, any observed difference could be dismissed as noise.

claims.claim: Stop or redesign when degree-preserving randomized cross-plane edges perform equivalently.
claims.why: Falsifiable if 'equivalently' is defined (e.g., within a margin). Without an equivalence margin and a statistical test (e.g., TOST), the claim is ambiguous.

claims.claim: Stop or redesign when four independent indices perform equivalently to cross-plane fusion.
claims.why: Same issue as 13.2; 'perform equivalently' needs a quantitative definition.

claims.claim: Stop or redesign when a plane has no marginal contribution in ablation.
claims.why: Falsifiable if 'no marginal contribution' is defined as below a threshold (e.g., <1% improvement). Without a threshold, the claim is vague.

claims.claim: Stop or redesign when graph movement does not predict or cause behavioral improvement.
claims.why: Falsifiable if 'predict or cause' is operationalized (e.g., correlation coefficient, causal intervention). The claim mixes prediction and causation, which require different experimental designs.

claims.claim: Stop or redesign when graph-conditioned prioritization does not beat random or evaluator-only choice.
claims.why: Falsifiable but needs a significance criterion and a fixed baseline (e.g., random seed). Without them, the comparison is ambiguous.

claims.claim: Stop or redesign when the gain disappears after temporal and knowledge-leakage scrubbing.
claims.why: Falsifiable if the scrubbing procedure is specified and 'disappears' is quantified (e.g., gain <1%). Without these, the claim is not testable.

claims.claim: Stop or redesign when extra context tokens explain the whole gain.
claims.why: Falsifiable if 'explain the whole gain' means that adding random tokens of equal length yields the same improvement. But the phrasing is ambiguous.

claims.claim: Stop or redesign when graph construction/query cost worsens the quality/cost frontier.
claims.why: Falsifiable if the frontier is defined (e.g., Pareto frontier) and 'worsens' is quantified (e.g., >10% degradation in quality per unit cost). Without a metric, it's subjective.

claims.claim: Stop or redesign when revision-atomic snapshots cannot be maintained at usable cost.
claims.why: Falsifiable if 'usable cost' is defined (e.g., <1% of total compute budget). Without a definition, it's subjective.

claims.claim: Stop or redesign when embedding proposals cannot achieve useful precision after verification cost.
claims.why: Falsifiable if 'useful precision' and 'verification cost' are quantified (e.g., precision >90% at cost <10% of query budget). Without numbers, it's vague.

claims.claim: Stop or redesign when benefits disappear on held-out repositories, under equal context budgets, or in cross-project transfer.
claims.why: Falsifiable if 'disappear' is quantified (e.g., gain <5%) and the conditions are specified. The claim lists three conditions, but it's unclear whether all must fail or just one.

claims.claim: For every comparative campaign, seal the evaluator from the candidate.
claims.why: This is a methodological instruction, not a kill criterion. It is falsifiable in the sense that one can check if it was followed.

claims.claim: Use identical problem definitions and compute/token budgets.
claims.why: Falsifiable: one can check if budgets and problem definitions match.
Falsifiable if 'multiple' is defined (e.g., at least 3). Otherwise, it's vague.

claims.claim: Run at least 5–10 seeds when stochastic variance matters.
claims.why: Falsifiable: one can check if the number of seeds is in the range.

claims.claim: Report algorithm quality, sample efficiency, repository evolution, and product reliability separately.
claims.why: Falsifiable: one can check if the report includes these metrics.

claims.claim: Reject results when code, prompts, memory, model, search policy, and evaluator changed together.
claims.why: Falsifiable: one can check if changes were made simultaneously.

claims.claim: Prevent leakage from gold patches, private tests, post-cutoff issue/commit text, post-task graph edges, previous solutions in adaptive memory, base/candidate snapshot mixing, evaluator paths or outputs, and model-generated hypotheses re-entering the Knowledge plane as facts.
claims.why: Partially falsifiable: some items (gold patches, private tests) are checkable with known methods. Others, like 'model-generated hypotheses re-entering the Knowledge plane as facts', are vague and lack a detection mechanism.
